# swarmops ws rebase

Move a workspace's chain onto its target's head, and its files with it.

On a conflict the workspace holds markers: edit them, ws resolve, then ws rebase --continue. --abort leaves the rebase and restores the conflicting paths.

```yaml
title: "swarmops ws rebase"
description: "Move a workspace's chain onto its target's head, and its files with it."
group: "workspaces"
since: "0.3.0"
mutates: true
identity_required: false
mcp_tool: "ws_rebase"
envelope_op: "ws_rebase"
exit_codes: [0, 1, 3]
errors: [E_CONFLICT, E_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICTS]
syntax: "swarmops ws rebase [OPTIONS]"
```

## Syntax

```text
swarmops ws rebase [OPTIONS]
```

## Required arguments

None.

## Optional arguments

The command also takes the [global options](../cli.md#global-options).

### `--ws`

Syntax: `--ws <NAME>`.

The workspace, by its name in the store's registry (default: the one around the working directory).

### `--ws-path`

Syntax: `--ws-path <DIR>`.

The workspace's directory.

### `--onto`

Syntax: `--onto <REF>`.
Default: `main`.

The ref to rebase onto: main or release/&lt;name&gt;, and in a FORMAT 2 store a branch (feature/x) or a tag (tags/v1).

### `--message`

Syntax: `-m, --message <MSG>`.

Commit the workspace's edits first, with this message (default: edits are E\_WS\_DIRTY).

### `--continue`

Syntax: `--continue`.

Rebase again once the conflicts are resolved.

### `--abort`

Syntax: `--abort`.

Leave the rebase.

### `--status-after`

Syntax: `--status-after <STATUS_AFTER>`.
Default: `page`.

page: the first page of the status follows the result; none: it is left out. Values: `page`: The first page of the status; `none`: No status.

## Examples

### CLI

```sh
swarmops --repo [tmp]/store --as agent/worker-17 ws rebase --ws w2 --onto release/ws
```

Exit code 3. Recorded by the CLI tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time.

## Return information

`result` is a `WsRebaseResp` (`swarmops schema WsRebaseResp` prints its JSON Schema).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `changeset` | `string` | yes | The workspace's head now. |
| `onto` | `string` | yes | The target's head it was rebased onto. |
| `status` | `RebaseStatus or null` | no | How the rebase ended; `None` after an abort. |
| `status_after` | `WsStatus or null` | no | The status after the mutation; omitted when the request said `none`. |

Envelope `op`: `ws_rebase`.

Exit codes:

- `0`: Success.
- `1`: The operation failed.
- `3`: The change conflicts with what it lands on: resolve it, then run the operation again.

## Errors

- [`E_CONFLICT`](../errors.md#e_conflict) (exit 3): The change conflicts with the target: `details.report` lists each conflicting file with its kind, its hunks and who changed it on the target.
- [`E_UNRESOLVED_CONFLICTS`](../errors.md#e_unresolved_conflicts) (exit 1): A rebase still has conflicting paths no one resolved (`details.paths`).

Any command that opens a store may also fail with a store error, such as [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo), [`E_IO`](../errors.md#e_io) or [`E_STORE_CORRUPT`](../errors.md#e_store_corrupt); a command line the grammar refuses is [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg) (exit 2).
